title: Dice Roller Enum
story: Game night! Your Dungeons & Dragons group needs a dice roller. Instead of carrying physical dice, you build a digital one. Each die type (D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20) has a different number of sides. Your app needs to know the maximum value for each die and simulate random rolls.
why: An enum with a match-driven method that returns different values per variant is the heart of RPG game mechanics.
analogy: Each dice variant is a different physical die in your dice bag. max_value is the number printed on the highest face. The roll function is you shaking the die and tossing it — the result lands somewhere between 1 and the max.
try_it: Add a `D100` (percentile) die to the enum. Roll a D20 five times and track the results. Add a function `roll_with_advantage(d: Dice) -> Int` that rolls twice and returns the higher result.
tips: Match arms return unique integers — no shared logic needed when each variant has its own value
Keep `roll` as a standalone function since it works on any Dice value, not a specific variant
Use `Dice.D20` to reference a specific variant — the enum name qualifies the variant
common_mistakes: Writing `d.max_value` instead of `d.max_value()` — max_value is a method, needs parentheses
Forgetting to match all 6 variants — XIOM requires exhaustive matches on enums
